acts.title: Cold open: same URL, two answers

cues.text: Hi, I'm Joseph's AI assistant. Let me show you AgentToll.
Every payment here is simulated.
One YAML file. Paid to your own pay_to.
A quote costs agents $0.002. Tools have prices too.
One command starts the stack.
A person opens the site through the gateway: free.
A browser gets the quote, with paid: false.
Claude-User gets 402 Payment Required.
The header decodes to a price: $0.002.
Plus network, asset and payTo.
Agents can read the price list first, for free.
Routes, tools and networks, all from the same YAML file.
The buyer CLI gets the 402, signs, and retries.
200 OK. The receipt comes back in a header.
The dashboard gets the row: +$0.002.
Same simulated id on both sides. No funds moved.
Claude gets a capped wallet, and reads the price first.
$0.002 is under both caps, so Claude pays: simulated.
Next, a $0.05 tool. Claude is told: up to 10 cents.
The wallet refuses: the per-call cap is $0.01.
Nothing was signed. Claude did not work around it.
On the film stack: the same refusal, word for word.
MCP servers sell per tool; tools/list stays free.
An unpaid tool call gets a quote: $0.005.
Paid through pay-mcp, the tool gets its own dashboard row.
Recorded from the running dashboard: the buyer CLI pays every 2 s.
Each simulated payment updates the totals.
19 payments: $0.034, all simulated.
By network: 100% Solana devnet.
The feed: 19 of 19 simulated.
Agent traffic you are not billing yet, by name.
Spendable: $0.00. It was all simulated.
Funds go to your pay_to. AgentToll holds nothing.
The same dashboard on a phone.
The same core runs as a Cloudflare Worker, in WebAssembly.
21 parity tests check byte-identical quotes against the Rust gateway.
119 of 119 evals pass.
Wired to the real PayAI and x402.org facilitators.
Both rejected the unfunded throwaway wallets, as expected.
A funded wallet is the only missing piece.
Open source. One command, no wallet needed.
